approach: Method development and validation study. Cell lysates were prepared from PBMCs, RBCs, and DBS. Nucleotides were separated by charge using anion-exchange solid-phase extraction (QMA cartridges). Triphosphate fractions were enzymatically dephosphorylated to nucleosides using alkaline phosphatase. Analytes were purified via phenylboronic acid (PBA) SPE and quantified using LC-MS/MS in positive electrospray ionization mode. Validation included assessment of linearity, intra-/inter-assay precision and accuracy, matrix effects, recovery, process efficiency, conditional stability (freeze/thaw, room temperature, extracted), carryover, and cross-talk. Clinical application involved comparing MP vs. TP levels in PBMCs, PBMCs vs. RBCs, and paired RBC vs. DBS samples from 36 hepatitis C patients treated with ribavirin.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Provides a validated LC-MS/MS method that avoids ion-suppression issues of ion-pairing HPLC by using dephosphorylation and simple aqueous mobile phases. Enables simultaneous quantification of MP and TP forms in multiple blood cell matrices.
contribution_and_limits.limits: The method is susceptible to environmental contamination (e.g., bacteria, dust) which affects the Lower Limit of Quantification (LLOQ), particularly for IMP/ITP. The utility of DBS for accurate nucleotide quantification is limited by instability/hydrolysis of TPs during sample processing and storage, requiring further evaluation or immediate processing protocols.

key_findings.conditions: Validation in PBMCs, RBCs, and DBS matrices
key_findings.finding: The assay demonstrated linear ranges of 10–2000 pmol/sample for ATP, 1.0–200 pmol/sample for GTP, and 0.25–50 pmol/sample for ITP. Intraassay precision (%CV) ranged from 1.7% to 16%, and interassay precision was within similar bounds. Accuracy (%deviation) was between -11.5% and 14.7%.

key_findings.conditions: Comparison of cell types (PBMCs vs. RBCs)
key_findings.finding: Nucleotide levels in PBMCs were significantly higher than in RBCs: 10-fold for ATP, 55-fold for GTP, and 5.6-fold for ITP. Monophosphate concentrations were generally lower than triphosphate concentrations, except for inosine.

key_findings.conditions: Comparison of DBS vs. Paired RBC Lysates
key_findings.finding: DBS samples showed an average of 26% lower triphosphate (TP) levels and 184% higher monophosphate (MP) levels compared to paired RBC lysates, suggesting hydrolysis of TPs to MPs during the DBS drying and storage process.

Analytes were stable through freeze/thaw cycles and in extracted form at room temperature for up to 6 days. However, samples in methanol/water lysate were unstable at room temperature for extended periods (>2 hours), particularly for GTP at low concentrations.

problem_or_question: To develop a sensitive, specific, and robust bioanalytical method capable of simultaneously measuring physiologically relevant concentrations of MP and TP forms of adenosine, guanosine, and inosine in various clinical sample types (PBMCs, RBCs, DBS), addressing limitations of previous HPLC-UV methods such as ion suppression and inability to easily distinguish phosphorylation states without complex mobile phases.
research_scope: Human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), red blood cells (RBCs), and dried blood spots (DBS) from hepatitis C-infected individuals; quantification of endogenous adenosine, guanosine, and inosine nucleotides.
work_summary: This study developed and validated a liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) method for the simultaneous quantification of adenosine, guanosine, and inosine mono- (MP) and triphosphate (TP) forms in human cellular matrices. The method employs solid-phase extraction followed by enzymatic dephosphorylation to convert nucleotides into their parent nucleoside forms for detection, thereby simplifying chromatography and avoiding ion suppression associated with ion-pairing agents. The assay was validated for accuracy, precision, linearity, and stability across PBMCs, RBCs, and DBS matrices using samples from 36 patients. Key findings include higher nucleotide concentrations in PBMCs compared to RBCs, significant hydrolysis of triphosphates to monophosphates in DBS samples during storage/drying, and identification of environmental contamination as a critical factor limiting the lower limit of quantification for certain analytes.
